:::{#thm-hessian-forms}
#### Other ways to write the Hessian, and its entries

Let $f$ and $\vx$ be as in @def-hessian.

1. The Hessian can be written with the row-vector derivative (@def-row-vector-derivative) of $f$:

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \matr{H}_f(\vx)
   &= \deriv{\vx} \paren{\derivf{f(\vx)}{\tp{\vx}}} \\
   &= \xderivf{f(\vx)}{\vx}{\tp{\vx}}.
   \end{aligned}
   $$ {#eq-hessian-row}

2. The $(i, j)$ entry of the Hessian is

   $$
   \sb{\matr{H}_f(\vx)}_{ij} = \deriv{x_i} \paren{\deriv{x_j} f(\vx)}.
   $$ {#eq-hessian-entry}

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

**Part 1.**
By @thm-row-deriv-tp-col-deriv, the transposed gradient $\tp{\paren{\deriv{\vx} f(\vx)}}$
equals the row-vector derivative $\derivf{f(\vx)}{\tp{\vx}}$.
Substituting it into @eq-hessian gives the first line.
The second line is the same expression written as a second derivative.
It follows the shape rule of matrix multiplication (@rem-row-derivative-shape):
the $p \times 1$ column-vector operator $\deriv{\vx}$ stands on the left of a $1 \times p$ row vector,
giving a $p \times p$ matrix.

**Part 2.**
Let $y_j \eqdef \deriv{x_j} f(\vx)$ be entry $j$ of the gradient.
By @def-vector-valued-derivative, the $(i, j)$ entry of the derivative of the vector $\vy = (y_1, \ldots, y_p)$
with respect to $\vx$ is

$$
\ba
\sb{\matr{H}_f(\vx)}_{ij}
&= \sb{\deriv{\vx} \tp{\vy}}_{ij}
&& \text{(@eq-hessian, with } \vy \text{ the gradient)}
\\
&= \deriv{x_i} y_j
&& \text{(@def-vector-valued-derivative)}
\\
&= \deriv{x_i} \paren{\deriv{x_j} f(\vx)}.
&& \text{(} y_j = \deriv{x_j} f(\vx) \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

:::
